en.html:
Higekiri shot into the rear approach. A small gap behind him—but definitely behind—I followed.

His escape route I had blocked. At the beginning. Even when we stopped his acrobatics and began pressing him, that one entrance should have been behind me.

Then when—WHEN!

...While we were measuring the distance against each other!?

One last counterattack, that was what he made me think he was preparing. An escape route he had actually been arranging!!

He was right. Lost in the fighting, I had forgotten the whole situation.

Finish the opponent quickly—that requirement was mine alone. He only had to leave this underground space alive. His victory conditions, all satisfied!

That much I had forgotten.

No... perhaps the terrifying part was that the Grand Commander had remembered. An unknown attacker threatening his life, and still such a cool head.

This was the difference between a raw boy and an old campaigner, was it?

en.html:
Bodies everywhere.

Soldiers.
Armored warriors.
Attendants.
Priests.

The shogunate's people on the surface. The people of Hachiman Shrine. No distinction left. Such complete equality: the same death had been given to every one.

Life, none.
Quietly, smoothly, a world at peace had appeared.

An ice field, this was.
The wilderness of the far north.

Beginning and end together. A closed, three-dimensional world. It would not move. It would not change.

en.html:
Not one glance for the Grand Commander.
Straight at me she turned her face.

Hikaru.

...Two years it had been.
Since I had seen her unarmored, this close.

With that much time gone, at that age, so little change I would never have expected. Almost the same figure as in my memory. It left me feeling strangely out of step.

Why so little change?
Why so much like before?

When Hikaru's fate—her star—had changed so terribly!

Silver Star spat the words out. Arms folded, thoroughly annoyed.

A conversation had failed to please her. That much aftermath, nothing more. No sign that a battle had even happened.

Higekiri's strength I had just learned for myself. An ancient masterpiece, an experienced pilot: a formidable armored warrior. She had defeated that warrior.

Not one breath out of place.

Silver Star.

This monster.
This Silver Star—this Hikaru—I had to defeat.

...My brain was frozen, but the minimum judgment still had to be made.

Could I win?
Against this monster, with strength on an entirely different scale?

With my strength—

　しかし、勝てるのか。
　余りにも桁が違い過ぎるこの怪物に、勝てるか。

　俺の力で――
